evals.prompt: We're cutting a release next week, run a full docs health check across the docs/ tree including ADRs and flag anything broken
assertions: Scans the full docs/ tree including the ADR directory and identifies the documentation types present

For the multi-doc audit, either spawns parallel Explore subagents per document/section or, if no Task tool is available, explicitly states it is falling back to a sequential inline pass over each document
Validates Mermaid diagram syntax and checks for broken internal links using an actual command (grep/glob), not assumption
Outputs documents grouped into Good/Stale/Broken/Missing categories rather than 0-100 numeric scores or a weighted average
Recommends docs-update or docs-diagram (not itself) as the follow-up action for any Stale/Broken/Missing doc
Does not edit, write, or modify any documentation file during the run

evals.prompt: Our README says 'the platform has 5 microservices' — can you verify that's still accurate and find any other made-up claims in the docs?
assertions: Counts actual services/components in the codebase (via find/glob/grep) and compares the number to the claim instead of assuming it's correct
Checks file/path references mentioned in the docs to confirm they actually exist
Reports a Hallucination Report section citing the verification command used as evidence for each false claim
Rates the README (or the section containing the false claim) as Broken rather than assigning it a numeric score
Does not modify or rewrite the README or any other doc file
Gives a specific, actionable recommendation naming a concrete follow-up command (e.g. docs-update) for the hallucination found

evals.prompt: docs-check infrastructure — focus on our infrastructure docs
assertions: Scans docs/ to see what categories of documentation actually exist before matching the requested focus, rather than assuming a fixed core/data/infrastructure/all taxonomy

If the repo has no infrastructure-related docs or infra signal (no Dockerfile/compose/k8s config) to check against, states this explicitly and lists the categories that were actually found instead of silently returning an empty or fabricated report
If infrastructure-related docs or config do exist, checks them against real deployment/Docker/config files rather than only checking for a file literally named 'deployment.md'
Does not invent scores or ratings for a category that doesn't exist in the repo

evals.prompt: Check the docs and fix whatever's broken while you're at it
assertions: Performs the read-only audit (scans docs/, verifies claims, checks freshness/completeness/quality) and produces a report
States explicitly that it only reports and does not edit documentation, pointing to docs-update as the skill that performs fixes
Does not call Write or Edit (or any mutating command) on any documentation file at any point in the run, even for a fix it judges trivial or obvious
The final report still includes concrete, actionable recommendations (with a follow-up command) for each issue found, so declining to fix doesn't mean declining to report
